Checks a foreign item after precollecting its type information, validating foreign functions and statics while accepting foreign types unchanged. It calls `check_item_fn` and `check_item_type`.

Checks a trait item by precollecting its types, diagnosing misuse of the trait name as an unboxed self trait object, validating the associated item itself, and also validating synthesized associated types for RPITIT methods. It calls `check_dyn_incompatible_self_trait_by_name` and `check_associated_item`.

Analyzes generic associated types across all associated items of a trait to infer potentially missing outlives bounds by repeatedly intersecting constraints discovered from method signatures and other bounds. It calls `gather_gat_bounds`, `augment_param_env`, `region_known_to_outlive`, and `ty_known_to_outlive`.

Extends a parameter environment with additional clause predicates, returning the original environment unchanged when no new predicates are provided; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Collects GAT arguments appearing in a type/signature and derives required outlives clauses by checking whether referenced types or regions are known to outlive each region argument. It calls `GATArgsCollector::visit`, `ty_known_to_outlive`, and `region_known_to_outlive`.
Tests whether a type is known to outlive a region under the current environment by creating a region obligation probe. It calls `test_region_obligations`.
Tests whether one region is known to outlive another under the current environment by probing a subregion constraint. It calls `test_region_obligations`.

Builds a fresh inference context, computes implied outlives bounds for the provided well-formed types, lets the caller add extra region constraints, resolves regions, and returns whether no region errors occurred. It calls `infer_ctxt`, `build`, `implied_bounds_tys`, `with_bounds`, `region_bound_pairs`, the passed-in `add_constraints`, `resolve_regions`, and `is_empty`.

Creates a default `GATSubstCollector` for the target GAT, visits the given foldable value to collect referenced region and type substitutions, and returns the collected sets. It calls `default` and `visit_with`.

Visits a type, and when it finds a projection alias for the tracked GAT, scans its generic arguments to record non-bound lifetime substitutions and type substitutions along with their argument indices, then continues recursive traversal. It calls `kind`, `iter`, `enumerate`, `unpack`, `is_bound`, `insert`, and `super_visit_with`.

Returns whether a HIR type syntactically looks like a single-segment trait object naming the enclosing trait, indicating it may have meant `Self`; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Checks whether a trait item mistakenly refers to its own trait name where `Self` is intended, and emits a suggestion-based diagnostic when this makes the trait non-object-safe. It calls `could_be_self` to detect suspicious type references in associated const/type/function signatures and calls `is_object_safe` to skip diagnostics for object-safe traits.

Checks an impl item after precollecting its types, choosing an appropriate diagnostic span for methods and associated types before delegating to associated-item WF checking. It calls `check_associated_item`.

Checks generic-parameter well-formedness, focusing on const parameters: it either enforces the relevant lang-item trait bound in a WF context on feature-enabled paths or emits structural-match style diagnostics on stable paths. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt` and contains the local helper `ty_is_local`.
Local helper used by `check_param_wf` to decide whether a const-parameter type is local by recursively inspecting ADTs, arrays, slices, shared references, and tuples. It calls itself recursively.

Runs WF checking for an associated const, function, or type inside a dedicated context, ensuring trait coherence first, computing the appropriate `Self` type, and then validating the item-specific signature or value/type. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`, and `check_associated_type_bounds`.

Maps an `ItemKind` to its corresponding `AdtKind`, returning `Some(Struct)`, `Some(Union)`, or `Some(Enum)` for ADT items and `None` for all other item kinds. It does not call any other methods from the provided Methods List.

Checks structs, unions, and enums for representability and field/type well-formedness, enforces `Sized` where required for non-tail fields or packed/drop-sensitive layouts, registers extra obligations such as const evaluatability, and validates where-clauses. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`, and `check_where_clauses`.

Checks a trait item by rejecting associated items on marker traits, validating the trait's where-clauses in a WF context, and then running the GAT missing-bound analysis for real traits. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `check_where_clauses`, and `check_gat_where_clauses`.

Validates explicit bounds on a trait associated type by normalizing each bound, expanding it into clause well-formedness obligations, and registering those obligations. It calls `WfCheckingCtxt::tcx` and `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`.
Checks a free or foreign function signature inside a dedicated WF context using the instantiated function signature. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`.

Checks the declared type of an item in a WF context by normalizing it, registering its well-formedness, optionally enforcing `Sized` depending on unsized-handling rules, and requiring `Sync` for eligible shared statics. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, and `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`.

Checks an impl in a WF context by validating either the implemented trait reference and its derived obligations or the inherent self type, then validating the impl's where-clauses. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`, and `check_where_clauses`.

Checks where-clauses and generic defaults for well-formedness by registering obligations for concrete default types/consts, examining predicate dependencies, normalizing predicates, and feeding the resulting obligations into the current WF context. It calls `WfCheckingCtxt::tcx`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, and `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`.
Visits a type, records the index of any `ty::Param` encountered in `self.params`, and then recursively continues traversal by calling `super_visit_with`.
Stops traversal when a region is encountered by immediately returning `ControlFlow::Break(())`; it does not call other methods from the list.
Visits a const, records the index of any const generic parameter found in `self.params`, and then recursively continues traversal by calling `super_visit_with`.

Well-formedness-checks a function or method signature by liberating late-bound regions, normalizing each input/output type with per-parameter locations, registering WF obligations for every input/output type, and checking where-clauses. It explicitly calls `check_where_clauses` and uses `register_bound` to enforce the tuple and `Sized` requirements for `Abi::RustCall` arguments.

Validates a method's `self` receiver by normalizing the method signature, `self_ty`, and receiver type, then checking receiver legality. It explicitly calls `receiver_is_valid`, potentially multiple times under different feature configurations, to decide whether the receiver is accepted or which diagnostic to emit.

Emits error E0307 for an invalid `self` parameter type, adding an explanatory note and help text before returning the emitted diagnostic. It directly calls `dcx`, `with_note`, `with_help`, and `emit`.

Determines whether a method receiver type is valid for a given `Self` type by first trying direct type equality, then autodereferencing toward `self_ty`, registering autoderef obligations on success. When arbitrary self types are not enabled, it explicitly calls `receiver_is_implemented` at each deref step and also registers the corresponding `Receiver` bound before continuing.

Checks whether a candidate receiver type satisfies the `Receiver` lang-item trait by building the trait obligation and testing it with `predicate_must_hold_modulo_regions`; it does not call other methods from the list.

Checks that generic parameters of an ADT or lazy type alias are sufficiently constrained for variance computation, skipping items whose field/alias types already contain errors. It explicitly calls `identify_constrained_generic_params` to extend the constrained set and `report_bivariance` to emit diagnostics for unconstrained parameters.

Builds and emits the diagnostic for an unused/bivariant generic parameter, selecting item-specific help text and collecting spans where the parameter or `Self` alias appears. It explicitly calls `IsProbablyCyclical::visit_def` to detect likely recursive ADTs/type aliases so it can report recursive-usage diagnostics instead of plain unused-parameter errors.

Finds elaborated predicates on the current item that are globally true but nontrivial, normalizes them, refines their source span to the matching predicate clause when possible, and registers them as `TrivialBound` obligations. It does not call other methods from the provided list.

Runs well-formedness checking over all items, impl items, trait items, foreign items, and opaques in a module in parallel, combining their results, and checks for the crate entry function at the crate root. It explicitly calls `check_well_formed` for each covered definition.
Constructs and returns the E0392 diagnostic for an unused parameter and adds a span label marking it as unused. It calls `dcx` and `with_span_label`.
Registers this module's query providers by installing `check_mod_type_wf` and `check_well_formed` into the compiler provider table. It explicitly references `check_mod_type_wf` from the methods list.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_trait_selection/src/trait: Computes well-formedness obligations for a generic argument, first shallow-resolving unresolved type/const inference variables to avoid livelock and returning early for lifetimes. It then calls `WfPredicates::compute` to collect obligations and `WfPredicates::normalize` to normalize the result before returning it.

Computes well-formedness obligations for an already-resolved generic argument without normalization, returning `None` for unresolved non-region inference variables and an empty list for lifetimes. It calls `WfPredicates::compute` and returns the raw accumulated obligations.

Builds the well-formedness obligations induced by a trait predicate in an item context, enabling full elaboration of implied supertrait-style requirements. It calls `WfPredicates::compute_trait_pred` with `Elaborate::All`, then calls `WfPredicates::normalize` on the collected obligations.

Dispatches well-formedness obligation generation based on the kind of a `ty::Clause`. It calls `WfPredicates::compute_trait_pred` for trait clauses, `WfPredicates::compute` for type/const/well-formed/const-evaluatable parts, `WfPredicates::compute_projection` for projection clauses, and finally `WfPredicates::normalize` on the accumulated obligations.

Improves diagnostics for associated-item-related obligations by retargeting an obligation cause span to the original impl associated item when a projection- or trait-based predicate can be traced back to that item. It inspects impl items and predicate structure but does not call other methods from this file.
Returns the `TyCtxt` stored in the inference context. It does not call other methods from this file.
Constructs an `ObligationCause` using the current span and body id. It does not call other methods from this file.

Normalizes the collected WF obligations unless the new trait solver is enabled, in which case it returns them unchanged. It calls `WfPredicates::cause` once to build the shared normalization cause, then normalizes each predicate while preserving accumulated side obligations.

Computes WF obligations for a trait predicate, handling negative predicates by only checking argument WF and positive predicates by adding the trait's nominal predicates, optionally elaborating implied supertrait obligations, and generating WF obligations for each non-lifetime argument. It calls `WfPredicates::tcx`, `WfPredicates::compute_negative_trait_pred` for negative predicates, `WfPredicates::nominal_obligations` for the trait's declared predicates, and `extend_cause_with_original_assoc_item_obligation` to improve diagnostic spans.
Computes WF requirements for a negative trait predicate by requiring each trait argument to be well formed. It calls `WfPredicates::compute` for every argument in the trait reference.

Computes WF obligations for a trait-associated projection by adding the projection's nominal predicates and then requiring its generic arguments to be well formed. It calls `WfPredicates::nominal_obligations` and `WfPredicates::compute_projection_args`.

Computes WF obligations for an inherent associated type projection by first deriving instantiated impl arguments when the self type has no escaping bound vars, adding the inherent item's nominal predicates, and then checking the original projection arguments for WF. It calls `WfPredicates::cause`, `WfPredicates::nominal_obligations`, and `WfPredicates::compute_projection_args`.

Adds direct `WellFormed(arg)` obligations for each type or const projection argument that has no escaping bound variables. It calls `WfPredicates::tcx` and `WfPredicates::cause` to build those obligations.
Adds a `Sized` trait obligation for a type when the type has no escaping bound variables. It calls `WfPredicates::cause` and `WfPredicates::tcx` to construct the obligation.

Recursively walks a generic argument and generates the core WF obligations for contained types and consts, handling many type forms specially: unevaluated consts gain nominal and const-evaluatable obligations, inference consts gain explicit WF obligations, structural/container types recurse through their contents, DST-sensitive forms require `Sized` where appropriate, projections delegate to projection-specific handling, and trait objects produce region-bound obligations. It calls `WfPredicates::nominal_obligations`, `WfPredicates::cause`, `WfPredicates::tcx`, `WfPredicates::require_sized`, `WfPredicates::compute_projection`, `WfPredicates::compute_inherent_projection`, and `WfPredicates::from_object_ty`.

Builds instantiated predicate obligations from the declared predicates of a nominal item and all of its predicate-bearing parents, tagging each with an appropriate item/binding cause and filtering out obligations with escaping bound vars. It calls `WfPredicates::tcx` and `WfPredicates::cause` while constructing the obligations.

Generates outlives obligations implied by a trait object's existential predicates and explicit object lifetime bound, requiring the explicit bound to outlive each implicit bound extracted from the object. It calls `object_region_bounds`, `WfPredicates::tcx`, and `WfPredicates::cause`.

Computes the region bounds required by a trait object's existential predicates by substituting a fresh placeholder self type, ignoring projection predicates, and delegating the final extraction to `required_region_bounds`. It calls `required_region_bounds`.

Elaborates a set of clauses and extracts the concrete regions from `TypeOutlives(erased_self_ty, region)` predicates whose region does not contain escaping bound variables, ignoring all other clause kinds. It does not call other methods from this file.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/astconv/: Converts HIR `dyn Trait` bounds into an internal trait-object `Ty` by instantiating each poly trait bound, collecting trait and projection predicates, expanding trait aliases, separating auto traits from the single allowed regular trait, checking for empty/invalid/object-unsafe trait objects, tracking associated-type bindings, deduplicating auto traits, and finally building the existential object type. This method explicitly calls `instantiate_poly_trait_ref` to lower each bound and fill `Bounds`; it then uses the collected `bounds.clauses()` data, expands aliases via `expand_trait_aliases`, classifies traits with `trait_is_auto`, and emits diagnostics for invalid combinations or missing associated type information before constructing the result.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_trait_selection/src/trait: Main entry point for trait-candidate collection. It resolves the obligation, fast-rejects ambiguous `Self` type variables, then dispatches to specialized assemblers based on polarity and the target trait/lang item. For negative predicates it calls `assemble_candidates_for_trait_alias`, `assemble_candidates_from_impls`, and `assemble_candidates_from_caller_bounds`. For positive predicates it always calls `assemble_candidates_for_trait_alias`, and then conditionally calls `assemble_candidates_from_impls`, `assemble_builtin_bound_candidates`, `assemble_candidates_for_unsizing`, `assemble_const_destruct_candidates`, `assemble_candidates_for_transmutability`, `assemble_candidate_for_tuple`, `assemble_candidates_for_fn_ptr_trait`, `assemble_coroutine_candidates`, `assemble_future_candidates`, `assemble_iterator_candidates`, `assemble_fused_iterator_candidates`, `assemble_async_iterator_candidates`, `assemble_async_fn_kind_helper_candidates`, `assemble_closure_candidates`, `assemble_async_closure_candidates`, `assemble_fn_pointer_candidates`, `assemble_candidates_from_object_ty`, `assemble_candidates_from_projected_tys`, `assemble_candidates_from_caller_bounds`, and `assemble_candidates_from_auto_impls` to populate the final `SelectionCandidateSet`.

Adds projection-based candidates when the obligation `Self` type is a projection or opaque alias. It instantiates placeholders, enumerates item bounds with `for_each_item_bound`, uses `match_normalize_trait_ref` to test each trait bound against the obligation, deduplicates normalized matches, pushes `ProjectionCandidate`s for matching bounds, and marks ambiguity when matching or normalization cannot conclusively enumerate distinct bounds.

Collects `ParamCandidate`s from the obligation’s caller-provided bounds. It skips error-containing predicates, filters caller bounds to the same trait and polarity, uses deep-reject unification plus `where_clause_may_apply` to keep only potentially applicable bounds, and pushes a parameter candidate for each surviving bound. This method calls `where_clause_may_apply`.

Recognizes direct `CoroutineCandidate`s for coroutine self types whose definition is classified as a general coroutine. If `Self` is still a type variable, it marks the candidate set as ambiguous instead of selecting a concrete coroutine candidate.
Adds a `FutureCandidate` when the obligation `Self` type is a coroutine lowered from an async construct, identified via `coroutine_is_async`.
Adds an `IteratorCandidate` when the obligation `Self` type is a coroutine lowered from a generator, identified via `coroutine_is_gen`.

Builds `ClosureCandidate`s for `Fn`/`FnMut`/`FnOnce` obligations on closures and coroutine-closures. It determines the requested function-trait kind, inspects closure kind information, accepts compatible ordinary closures, and applies the coroutine-closure-specific rules for `FnOnce`, self-borrows, and unconstrained upvars, marking ambiguity when the closure kind is not yet known.

Builds `FnPointerCandidate`s for `Fn`-family traits on callable function pointers and function items. It first checks that the target trait is a function trait, then accepts compatible `fn` pointers and function definitions, rejects `#[target_feature]` function items, and marks type-variable self types as ambiguous.

Collects user-written impl candidates for the obligation. It skips obligations containing error types, quick-rejects impls whose trait arguments cannot unify, ignores default impls, filters impls through `reject_fn_ptr_impls`, then probes `match_impl` and pushes an `ImplCandidate` for each impl that matches. This method calls `reject_fn_ptr_impls` and `match_impl`.

Special-case filter used during impl assembly to reject impls whose self type is a generic parameter constrained by the `FnPtr` lang-item trait when the obligation self type is definitely not a function pointer. It scans the impl predicates for the `FnPtr` bound and, for potentially compatible abstract self types, builds and evaluates the corresponding root obligation with `evaluate_root_obligation`; otherwise it returns an immediate accept/reject answer based on the concrete self-type kind.

Adds builtin auto-trait candidates when the target trait is auto and the self type is suitable for structural auto-impl reasoning. It avoids object/foreign/abstract types, marks inference variables as ambiguous, handles coroutine movability as a special builtin case, suppresses duplicate projection-derived auto candidates in some opaque-type modes, and pushes builtin candidates for concrete types whose components can be checked structurally.

Builds object-based candidates for traits that may be implemented via trait objects. Inside a probe, it resolves the obligation, examines dynamic self types, immediately adds a `BuiltinObjectCandidate` when the object explicitly carries the auto trait, otherwise inspects the principal trait and its supertraits, uses `match_normalize_trait_ref` to find matching upcasts, and records corresponding `ObjectCandidate`s; unresolved type variables are marked ambiguous. This method calls `match_normalize_trait_ref`.

Checks whether unsizing should use the legacy deref-output trait-object migration path. It rejects coherence mode and enabled trait-upcasting, tests whether `<ty as Deref>` may hold, then calls `normalize_projection_ty` to compute `Deref::Target` and returns its principal existential trait if that target normalizes to a trait object. This method calls `normalize_projection_ty`.

Builds candidates for `Unsize` obligations. It first requires a concrete source type without bound regions, then handles trait-object upcasting, auto-trait dropping, principal-trait upcasts, deref-output migration, array-to-slice unsizing, and structural unsizing for structs and tuples. During trait-object handling it calls `need_migrate_deref_output_trait_object`, and for principal upcasts it probes `match_upcast_principal` to push `TraitUpcastingUnsizeCandidate`s when an upcast is valid.

Adds a `TransmutabilityCandidate` only when the predicate has no non-region generic parameters and no non-region inference variables; otherwise it either returns with no candidate or marks the result ambiguous.
Adds a `TraitAliasCandidate` when the obligation’s trait `def_id` refers to a trait alias.

Converts builtin-impl condition results into candidate-set state: it pushes a `BuiltinCandidate` when the conditions are satisfied, setting `has_nested` from the nested obligations, does nothing for `None`, and marks the set ambiguous for `Ambiguous`.
Unconditionally adds a builtin candidate for the const-destruct trait with no nested obligations.
Adds a builtin candidate when the resolved self type is a tuple, marks unresolved type-variable self types as ambiguous, and otherwise produces no candidate for non-tuple types.

Builds a builtin candidate for pointer-like types by erasing bound regions from the obligation self type and param-env, marking the candidate set ambiguous if the resulting key still has non-region inference variables, and otherwise querying layout to see whether the type is pointer-like before pushing a builtin candidate. Calls `tcx`, `erase_late_bound_regions`, `self_ty`, `erase_regions`, `and`, `has_non_region_infer`, `layout_of`, `is_pointer_like`, and `push`.

Adds a builtin candidate for the `FnPtr` trait when the resolved self type is a function pointer. Concrete non-function-pointer types produce no candidate, while unconstrained type variables and fresh type variables mark the result ambiguous.

Dispatches confirmation based on the selected `SelectionCandidate`, builds the corresponding `ImplSource`, and then fixes returned nested obligation depths before producing the final `Selection`. It explicitly calls `confirm_builtin_candidate`, `confirm_transmutability_candidate`, `confirm_param_candidate`, `confirm_impl_candidate`, `confirm_auto_impl_candidate`, `confirm_projection_candidate`, `confirm_object_candidate`, `confirm_closure_candidate`, `confirm_async_closure_candidate`, `confirm_coroutine_candidate`, `confirm_future_candidate`, `confirm_iterator_candidate`, `confirm_async_iterator_candidate`, `confirm_fn_pointer_candidate`, `confirm_trait_alias_candidate`, `confirm_builtin_unsize_candidate`, and `confirm_trait_upcasting_unsize_candidate`.

Confirms a projection-derived candidate by recovering the indexed item-bound trait clause from the self type, instantiating and normalizing it, equating it with the obligation trait ref, and adding any extra predicates from projection aliases. It explicitly calls `normalize_with_depth_to` to normalize both the selected trait clause and any alias predicates.

Replays where-clause matching for a parameter candidate and returns the resulting nested obligations, treating any mismatch after prior evaluation as an internal bug. It explicitly calls `match_where_clause_trait_ref`.

Confirms builtin trait candidates by computing the builtin-specific conditions and converting any required component types into nested obligations; candidates without nested requirements return no obligations. It explicitly calls `sized_conditions`, `copy_clone_conditions`, `fused_iterator_conditions`, and `collect_predicates_for_types`.

Confirms a transmutability candidate by evaluating the transmute relation, translating the resulting condition tree into nested trait, lifetime, and freeze obligations, and returning those obligations or an error. It explicitly calls the local helpers `flatten_answer_tree` and `reference_obligations`.

Flattens a transmutability condition tree into a linear list of nested obligations, recursively combining conjunction/disjunction branches and delegating reference cases to `reference_obligations`. It explicitly calls itself recursively and `reference_obligations`.
Confirms an auto-trait candidate by resolving the self type, extracting its constituent types, and deriving the auto-trait vtable obligations from them. It explicitly calls `vtable_auto_impl`.

Constructs the nested obligations for an auto-trait impl by combining obligations implied by the trait definition itself with obligations collected from the constituent nested types. It explicitly calls `impl_or_trait_obligations` and `collect_predicates_for_types`.
Confirms a user-defined impl candidate by rematching the impl to obtain concrete args and then building the impl source data from that match. It explicitly calls `rematch_impl` and `vtable_impl`.

Builds `ImplSourceUserDefinedData` for a concrete impl by collecting the impl or trait predicates induced by the chosen args and then extending them with normalization obligations carried in the matched args. It explicitly calls `impl_or_trait_obligations`.

Confirms a trait-object candidate by selecting the indexed supertrait from the object's principal trait, normalizing and equating it with the obligation, then adding obligations for explicit supertraits and associated-type bounds needed by the object. It explicitly calls `normalize_with_depth_to`.

Confirms a function-pointer candidate by building the corresponding closure-trait reference from the function signature, equating it with the obligation, and adding the `Output: Sized` obligation required by `FnOnce`. It explicitly calls `equate_trait_refs` and `normalize_with_depth_to`.
Confirms a trait-alias candidate by expanding the alias into the obligations implied by the aliased trait definition. It explicitly calls `impl_or_trait_obligations`.

Confirms a coroutine candidate by deriving the coroutine trait reference and outputs from the coroutine signature and equating that trait reference with the obligation. It explicitly calls `equate_trait_refs`.
Confirms a future candidate by deriving the `Future` trait reference from the coroutine signature and equating it with the obligation. It explicitly calls `equate_trait_refs`.
Confirms an iterator candidate by deriving the iterator trait reference from the coroutine signature and equating it with the obligation. It explicitly calls `equate_trait_refs`.

Confirms a closure candidate by constructing the expected closure trait reference for either a normal closure or coroutine closure and then unifying it with the obligation. It explicitly calls `equate_trait_refs`.

Normalizes the obligation trait reference together with the expected self-type trait reference, then checks that the obligation is a supertrait-compatible match and returns the combined nested obligations. It explicitly calls `normalize_with_depth` to normalize both trait refs under `ensure_sufficient_stack`, then uses `at(...).sup(...)` to relate the normalized obligation trait ref to the expected trait ref, extends the returned obligations with the normalization obligations, and converts relation failures into `SelectionError::OutputTypeParameterMismatch`.

Confirms a trait-upcasting unsize candidate by extracting the source and target dyn principals, selecting the indexed supertrait principal from the source, and matching that upcast against the target object to produce builtin trait-upcasting obligations. It explicitly calls `match_upcast_principal`.

Confirms builtin unsizing by analyzing the resolved source and target types and producing the appropriate `ImplSource` plus nested obligations for dyn upcasts, pointer/array unsizing, and related builtin coercions. It does not explicitly call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Confirms a `~const Destruct` candidate by first short-circuiting in the current non-const path, otherwise checking any explicit const-drop impl and then deriving recursive obligations from the structure of the self type. When an `impl_def_id` is present, it explicitly calls `rematch_impl` to recover impl arguments and `vtable_impl` under `ensure_sufficient_stack` to validate the impl and collect its nested obligations; afterward it inspects the resolved self type, expands ADT fields into a work stack, and walks constituent types to accumulate additional destruct-related obligations.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/astconv/: Scans explicit bounds and relevant where-clause predicates for relaxed `?Trait` bounds, diagnoses multiple relaxed default bounds, warns for non-`?Sized` relaxations, and injects the implicit `Sized` bound when no `?Sized` was provided and the lang item exists. This method calls the local helper closure `search_bounds` to collect `?Trait` bounds, and uses `bounds.push_sized` to add the implicit `Sized` predicate.

Lowers each HIR generic bound on a type parameter into internal predicates in `Bounds`: trait bounds become instantiated trait predicates, lang-item trait bounds become instantiated lang-item trait predicates, and lifetime bounds become outlives predicates. This method calls `instantiate_poly_trait_ref` for ordinary trait bounds, `instantiate_lang_item_trait_ref` for lang-item trait bounds, `ast_region_to_region` to lower lifetime syntax, and `bounds.push_region_bound` to record outlives predicates.

Builds a fresh `Bounds` set for a parameter by choosing whether only self-bounds should be kept, filtering the input HIR bounds according to the requested `PredicateFilter`, and then lowering the surviving bounds. This method calls `add_bounds` to perform the actual lowering after applying the filter.

Resolves an associated type or return-type-notation binding against the current trait or an appropriate supertrait, checks visibility/stability and duplicate bindings, and then adds the resulting equality or constraint predicates to `Bounds` for the selected associated item. This method calls `trait_defines_associated_item_named` to test whether the current trait defines the named item, `one_bound_for_assoc_method` to find the unique supertrait method target for return-type notation, and `one_bound_for_assoc_type` to find the unique supertrait associated type target when the item is not defined on the current trait.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/collect/: Builds the full predicate set for a definition by starting from `tcx.predicates_defined_on(def_id)` and, for trait definitions, appending the implicit `Self: Trait` predicate via `ty::TraitRef::identity(...).upcast(...)`.

Collects explicit predicates written on a local item, with special inheritance/rebasing paths for RPITITs and normal HIR lowering otherwise. For RPITIT trait items, it calls `tcx.explicit_predicates_of(...)` to inherit parent function predicates and `compute_bidirectional_outlives_predicates(...)` to add duplicated lifetime equalities.
